circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island designed by Hermann Tilke, has served as the Formula One season finale since 2009. The venue represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling a lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting motorsport events. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification status.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit originally operated as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. After undergoing reconstruction and shortening, the track was renamed and returned to hosting the Austrian Grand Prix in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit, a street track near Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan, spans 6. 003 km and ranks as the fourth-longest venue on the F1 calendar. The circuit hosted its first Formula One race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before transitioning to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix the following year, which became its permanent event.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km facility that hosted the first Formula One grand prix ever held in the Middle East, establishing itself as a premier motorsport venue with FIA Grade 1 status. The track has accommodated various racing series including GP2 and Australian V8 Supercars, along with endurance competitions, and features multiple configurable layouts.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit is renowned for its balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of driver and vehicle performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km Belgian circuit situated near the town of Spa in the Wallonia region, serving as the home of the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix. The track has hosted the Belgian Grand Prix continuously since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006, having first welcomed Formula One racing in 1950 during the championship's inaugural season.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Montreal's Notre Dame Island, this 4. 361-kilometer Canadian circuit serves as the home of the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various international motorsport series, including World Sportscar Championship events, open-wheel racing, and multiple NASCAR categories.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit is a motorsport venue most recognized for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track has expanded its racing calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix starting in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, this English circuit has been the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948 and hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After decades of rotating with two rival venues, the Grand Prix permanently established itself here from 1987 onward, while the track continues to welcome international motorcycle racing as well.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when racing commenced there in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One venue, the track was constructed outside the city after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected by authorities.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian racing facility constructed in 1922 near Milan, making it mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built circuit and only the third of its kind globally. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, the venue has earned the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its extended straights and fast-flowing turns that characterize high-speed racing.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: The Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km motorsport venue in Mie Prefecture, Japan, operated by Honda Mobilityland. It hosts major international racing events, most prominently the Formula One Grand Prix and the Japanese Super Formula championship, with a spectator capacity of 155,000.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that winds through Paradise, Nevada, following the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding urban landscape. The track passes by iconic entertainment venues and landmarks including MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it navigates the streets of the resort destination.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is named after two fatal racing drivers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The venue returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in 2015 after a 23-year absence, now running on a revised circuit layout distinct from its previous configurations used through 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 turns and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by specialist track engineers specifically for Formula One, the venue joined the championship calendar in 2022 as the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a compact 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, circumnavigating the harbour in Monaco's principality. Though officially named after Monaco, it is widely known as the Monte Carlo circuit due to its primary location within that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes west of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that rejoined the Formula One calendar in 2021 to host the revived Dutch Grand Prix. The partnership between the circuit and Formula One is scheduled to conclude following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a motor racing venue situated north of Doha in Qatar, featuring a 5. 419 km layout with a 1. 068 km main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features an associated karting facility bearing the name of racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that became the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix starting in 2021. The facility has since expanded its motorsport calendar to include Formula E racing from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront area, incorporating the city's core commercial district and the neighboring Kallang precinct into its racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657 km circuit in Montmeló features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for teams and drivers. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas spans 3. 426 miles and hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside NASCAR and motorcycle racing events. This FIA Grade 1 facility has also accommodated various other major motorsport series including IndyCar and sports car championships throughout its operational history.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver who currently represents Thailand in Formula One racing for the Williams team.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships during his 23-season career with 32 race victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both the Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli has been competing in Formula One since 2025, representing Mercedes as his team. He has achieved six race victories during his time in the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman represents Great Britain in Formula One, where he currently drives for Haas as an active competitor.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto is a Brazilian racing driver currently competing in the Formula One championship with Audi.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas is a Finnish Formula One driver currently racing for Cadillac. The driver achieved two runner-up finishes in the championship standings during 2019 and 2020 while at Mercedes, and has accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his 13-season career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor who currently races in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan holds a reserve role with Haas while pursuing his main racing programme in the European Le Mans Series with Nielsen Racing in the LMP2 category. He has made limited Formula One appearances, competing in seven races between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One competitor currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix during his time with AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, a driver with French and Algerian heritage who races under France's banner, currently competes in Formula One with Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding an unprecedented seven world championship titles that he shares with Michael Schumacher. The accomplished competitor leads the sport in multiple statistical categories, including most race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg is a German racing driver currently competing in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved notable success in endurance racing, claiming victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently driving for Racing Bulls in the Formula One championship.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc is a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari in Formula One, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career. He finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while racing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver competing in the World Endurance Championship with BMW and part-time in NASCAR, having returned to Formula One from 2022 to 2024 after an earlier stint in the sport from 2014 to 2020.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris represents Britain in Formula One's premier competition, currently driving for McLaren. The driver claimed the world championship in 2025 while with the team and has accumulated 12 race victories during his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. He achieved a significant career victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix when he drove for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac and brings extensive experience from 15 seasons of competition. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-year career in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo is an Australian driver who raced in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, earning the nickname "the Honey Badger" throughout his career. He achieved eight Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British racing driver, currently races for Mercedes in Formula One and has secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes in Formula One for Williams and has secured four Grand Prix victories during his 12-year career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following previous stints in IMSA endurance racing. His Formula One career spanned 2023 to 2024 before transitioning to international sports car racing.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Canadian driver Lance Stroll currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, competing at the highest level of international motorsport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, has been competing in Formula One since 2021 and currently holds a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls. His tenure in the sport spans from 2021 through 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch and Belgian racing driver competing for Red Bull Racing, Verstappen has secured four consecutive Formula One World Drivers' Championships between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12-season career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, the sole Chinese competitor in Formula One history, currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac. His racing career in the sport spanned from 2022 through 2024 as a full-time participant.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based Alpine team has competed in Formula One since 2021 as the rebranded works outfit of Renault, following the French manufacturer's decision to promote its Alpine sports car brand. Operating with a French licence and powered by Mercedes engines, the team secured its only victory during this era when Esteban Ocon triumphed at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, before Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of the 2025 season.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has maintained an intermittent presence in Formula One racing through different organizational structures, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco branding.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, with an unbroken presence in the championship since its inception in 1950. Nicknamed after their distinctive horse emblem, the squad has established itself as a dominant force throughout the sport's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas established this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, making its competitive debut in 2016. Under current team principal Ayao Komatsu, who took over from Guenther Steiner in early 2024, the squad continues as one of the grid's newer operations.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering firm earned acclaim in endurance racing, including overall victory at Le Mans in 1989, before entering Formula One as an independent constructor in 1993. After competing for over three decades and becoming the fourth-oldest constructor by races started, the team ceased operations in 2025 following its acquisition by Audi AG, which utilized its infrastructure to establish a new factory team.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited competes in Formula One under sponsorship agreements and operates from its headquarters at the McLaren Technology Centre in Woking, England. The team functions as part of the McLaren Group, which is owned by Bahrain's sovereign wealth fund.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes-Benz has maintained a significant presence in Formula One since 1954, operating as both a team owner and engine supplier across multiple periods. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas team, headquartered in Brackley and holding a German racing licence, became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff from January 2022, with the squad traditionally nicknamed the "Silver Arrows.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls, an Italian Formula One team and constructor, commenced operations in 2024 as the second racing division under Red Bull GmbH's ownership. Headquartered in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates alongside Red Bull Racing as part of the Austrian conglomerate's dual-team structure in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that launched in 2024 as the second Red Bull-owned outfit alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad operates under the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport division.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian licence from their English base, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 and has become one of two series entries owned by Red Bull GmbH. The team was led by Christian Horner throughout its two-decade tenure before Laurent Mekies assumed leadership in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's prior F1 venture, has become a cornerstone British constructor based in Grove, Oxfordshire. The team currently competes as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in the 2026 season. Operating from a substantial facility, Williams has maintained its position as a significant force in Formula One racing since its inception.
